title: MAX_CREDIT = 2 ceiling clamps the long-run rate of any type with cap > 2 — Thread 4's campus types cannot emit 'far more than a home'
evidence: spec:131-133: 'Credit is bounded at a **burst ceiling** `MAX_CREDIT = 2` (a terminal may burst up to 2 in a tick after idling; its long-run rate stays the cap — bounded short-spike honesty, no unbounded bursts).' · spec:151: '`cap(type) = CAP_FRACTION × throughput_units(type) ÷ packet_bandwidth`' · spec:254: 'a campus emits far more than a home' · spec:265: 'cap = CAP_FRACTION × throughput, uniform' · data/node_types.json: content_host throughput_units 80, router_high 160 (cap > 2 ⟺ throughput > 120).
detail: A token bucket with ceiling 2 and accrual > 2/tick saturates at 2 and spends at most 2/tick — long-run rate = min(cap, MAX_CREDIT), so 'long-run rate stays the cap' is false for exactly the high-throughput types Thread 4/card 5.11 introduce.
recommended_fix: Make the ceiling cap-relative (e.g. MAX_CREDIT = max(2, ceil(cap))) or per-type, and state the clamp rule for cap > MAX_CREDIT in Thread 2 + card 5.11.

title: MAX_CREDIT = 2 burst puts 60 u on the access at once — the second burst packet's access hop alone (12 ticks = 600 ms) exceeds email's 500 ms latency tolerance at the spec's own starting values
evidence: spec:131: 'a terminal may burst up to 2 in a tick after idling' · data/balance.json:6: 'transit ticks = ceil(packet_bandwidth / pipe.capacity_units)', packet_bandwidth 30 · data/packet_types.json email: '"latency_tol_ms": 500' · spec:157: residential cap '≈ 0.083 pkts/tick (2.5 u/s) — ~2× headroom vs the pre-5.10 narrow (5 u/s)' · stories-v2.md:677: '(W10) **one-subscriber-at-cap zero-drop** — a pinned test'.
detail: Burst 2 × 30 u = 60 u against the 5 u/s access: second packet serializes in 12 ticks = 600 ms (pre-5.10; 8 u/s post-5.10 leaves 400 ms before any downstream hop). Headroom math is average-rate only; W10 pins drops, never burst latency — self-inflicted SLA breach survives.
recommended_fix: Check MAX_CREDIT burst math against latency_tol in Thread 2/card 5.9: pin max access-hop serialization under burst ≤ the sourcing class's tolerance, or scale MAX_CREDIT down for low-throughput types.

title: State-home spec 'rebuilt by the spawn pass each tick' (the lane_caps pattern) contradicts cross-tick credit accumulation — a literal rebuild never lets a residential reach credit 1
evidence: spec:134-135: '**State home:** `spawn_credit[terminal_slot]` — a per-terminal buffer in the director's pressure state (demand.odin), slot-keyed like `lane_caps`, rebuilt by the spawn pass each tick.' vs spec:127-129: 'Each tick, every live terminal **accrues** `cap` credit ... a terminal is **pickable only while `credit >= 1`** ... sub-1 rates (residential ≈ 0.083/tick) are enforced exactly as "1 spawn per ~12 ticks"'.
detail: lane_caps is rebuilt-from-scratch as a pure function of current topology on gen change; the accumulator is history-dependent (idle time). A per-tick rebuild zeroes credit, so 0.083/tick never reaches 1 — eligible set permanently empty. Only 'advanced in place' reading works.
recommended_fix: Reword: 'carried in run state and advanced (accrued/spent) by the spawn pass each tick; resized on topology gen change like lane_caps' — never 'rebuilt'.

title: Group-bias draw's degenerate branches unspecified — no existing cluster (first growth spawn) and cluster at its group-size cap
evidence: spec:211-212: 'Growth (5.1) gains a **group-bias term** in the placement draw: a spawned terminal is drawn near an existing cluster member (a group radius + a group-size cap), so clusters actually concentrate.' — no other text covers the empty-cluster or at-cap branches; the conflict-resolution section covers only bias-vs-E31 ordering.
detail: The first growth spawn has no cluster member to bias toward (initial authored terminals' group membership is never defined), and a cluster reaching its size cap has no specified fallback (new group vs unbiased draw). Both branches are reachable every run.
recommended_fix: Specify: initial terminals seed groups (or the bias falls back to the unbiased draw until a cluster exists); an at-cap cluster starts a new group.
